4. Additional duties if customs.-(1) The additional duties of
customs on certain goods chargeable with a duty of customs under First Schedule
to the Tariff Act, 1934, or under the said Schedule read with any noti fication
of the Central Government for the time being in force, imposed up to 31st day
of March, 1943, by section 6 of the Finance Act, 1942, and continued, subject
to certain modifica tions up to the 31st day of March, 1949, by section 4 of
the Pakistan Finance Act, 1948, shall continue to be levied and collected as
provided in the said section 6, up to the 31st day of March, 1950, subject to
the modifications mentioned in sub section (2) XXXII of 1934, XII of 1942, I of
1948.
(2) The additional duties to be
levied and collected under the foregoing sub-section shall be:
one-half instead of one-fifth of
the amount of the duty of customs specified in the First Schedule to the Tariff
Act, 1934, in the case of toilet requisites not otherwise 3 specified (except
talcum powder, tooth powder, tooth paste, shaving soap and shaving cream)
comprised in item 28(14); fireworks, not otherwise specified, comprised in item
34(3); fabrics, not otherwise specified, containing more than 90 percent. of
silk, including such fabrics em broidered with artificial silk, comprised in
item 48; fabrics not otherwise specified, containing more than 90 per cent, of
artificial silk comprised in item 48 (1); fabrics, not otherwise specified,
containing more than 50 percent. of silk or artificial silk, or of both, and
not more than 90 percent. of silk, comprised in item 48(4)(a); fabrics
containing gold or silver thread, comprised in item 48(10); socks and stockings
made wholly or mainly from silk or artificial silk comprised in item 51;
articles, other than cutlery and surgical instruments, plated with gold or
silver, comprised in item 61(8); cutlery plated with gold or silver, comprised
in item 61(9); ivory, manufactured, not otherwise speci fied, comprised in item
82(1); toys, games, playing cards and all other articles comprised in item 84;
smoker's requisites excluding tobacco, and matches, comprised in item 85 (1).

7. Income-tax and super tax.-(1) Subject to the provisions of
sub-sections (3), (4), (5) and (6), for the year beginning on the 1st day of
April, 1949 -
(a) income-tax shall be charged
at the rates specified in Part I of the Fourth Schedule, and
(b) the rates of super-tax shall,
for the purposes of section 55 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, be those specified
in Part II of the Fourth Schedule, XI of 1922.
(2) In making any assessment for
the year ending on the 31st day of March, 1950, there shall be deducted from
the total income of an assessee, in accordance with the provisions of section
15A of the Income-tax Act, 1922, an amount equal to one-fifth of the earned
income, if any, included in his total in come, but not exceeding in any case
four thousand rupees XI of 1922.
(3) In making any assessment for
the year ending on the 31st day of March, 1950, where the total income of an
assessee, not being a company, includes any income chargeable under the head
"Salaries" as reduced by the deduction for earned income appropriate
thereto, or any income chargeable under the head "Interest on
securities", or any income from dividends in respect of which he is deemed
under section 49B of the Income-tax Act to have paid income-tax, the income-tax
payable by the assessee on that part of his total income which consists of such
inclusions shall be an amount bearing to the total amount of income-tax payable
according to the rates applicable under the operation of the Pakistan Finance
Act, 1948, on his total income the same proportion as the amount of such
inclusions bears to his total income I of 1948.
(4) In making any assessment for
the year ending on the 31st day of March, 1950, where the total income of an
assessee consists partly of earned income and partly of unearned income, the
super-tax payable by him shall be-
(i) on the earned income, the
amount which bears to the total amount of super-tax which would have been
payable on his total income had it consisted wholly of earned income the same
proportion as the earned income bears to his total income plus,
(ii) on the unearned income, the
amount which bears to the total amount of super-tax which would have been
payable on his total income had it consisted wholly of unearned income the same
proportion as the unearned income bears to his total income.
(5) In making any assessment for
the year ending on the 31st day of March, 1950,-
(a) where the total income of a
company includes any profits and gains from life insurance business the
super-tax payable by the company shall be reduced by an amount computed at the
rate of two annas in the rupee on that part of its total income which consist;
of such inclusion;
(b) where the total income of an
assessee, not being a company, includes any profits and gains from life
insurance business, the income-tax and super-tax payable by the assessee on
that part of his total income which consists of such inclusion shall be an
amount bearing to the total amount of such taxes payable according to the rates
applicable under the operation of the Finance Act, 1942, on his total income
the same proportion as the amount of such inclusion bears to his total income,
so however that the aggregate of the taxes so computed in respect of such
inclusion shall not in any case exceed the amount of tax payable on such inclu sion
at the rate of five annas in the rupee XII of 1942.
(6) In cases to which section 17
of the Income-tax Act, 1922, applies, the tax chargeable shall be determined as
provided in that section but with reference to the rates imposed by sub section
(1), and in accordance where applicable, with the provisions of sub-sections
(3), (4) and (5) of this section, XI of 1942.
